channel.title: Daily Digest
channel.description: A daily AI & tech news digest — curated, edited, published every morning.

item.title: Anthropic $50B Round
item.description: Anthropic is in discussions to raise a $40-50B funding round at an $850-900B valuation, more than doubling its $380B valuation from February. Sources say the company received multiple preemptive offers from investors eager to participate. The round could be its final private funding before a potential IPO. A board decision is expected in May.

item.title: AWS OpenAI Partnership
item.description: AWS announced a major expansion of its partnership with OpenAI, bringing the latest OpenAI models and Codex coding agent to Amazon Bedrock in limited preview. The partnership also includes Amazon Bedrock Managed Agents, enabling enterprises to build production-ready OpenAI-powered agents on AWS infrastructure. This comes one day after OpenAI and Microsoft revised their exclusivity terms.

item.title: Claude Outage
item.description: Claude.ai and the Anthropic API experienced a significant outage, leaving users unable to access the AI assistant. The incident garnered 110+ points on Hacker News with users reporting issues. The service has since been fixed.

item.title: Cursor Camp
item.description: Cursor Camp is a free interactive course that teaches developers how to effectively use Cursor, the AI-powered code editor. Created by Neal Agarwal (creator of Neal.fun and Popcorn), the course garnered 850+ points on Hacker News.

item.title: Google Pentagon Access
item.description: Google has granted the U.S. Department of Defense access to its AI for classified networks, allowing essentially all lawful uses. The deal follows Anthropic's public refusal to grant similar terms, after which the DoD branded Anthropic a "supply-chain risk." OpenAI and xAI signed deals immediately after Anthropic's refusal. 950 Google employees have signed an open letter asking the company to follow Anthropic's lead.

item.title: HERMES.md Bug
item.description: A bug in Claude Code causes API requests to route to metered endpoints when a file named HERMES.md exists in the project. The issue garnered 1,000+ points on Hacker News. Anthropic has acknowledged the bug and is working on a fix.

item.title: LocalSend
item.description: LocalSend is an open-source app that lets you send files between devices on the same network without internet. It works across platforms (Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android), making it a true cross-platform AirDrop alternative. The app garnered 900+ points on Hacker News.

item.title: Meta AI Spending
item.description: Meta has raised its full-year capital expenditure guidance to $125-145B, up from $115-135B, citing higher memory pricing and additional data center capacity needs. The company acknowledged it has "consistently underestimated" its compute needs. More than 8M advertisers now use at least one of Meta's AI creative tools, with video generation tool users seeing 3%+ higher conversion rates.

item.title: Mistral Medium 3.5
item.description: Mistral Medium 3.5 is an updated version of Mistral's medium-sized language model, featuring improved coding capabilities and reasoning. The model garnered 450+ points on Hacker News.

item.title: Nvidia Nemotron
item.description: Nemotron 3 Nano Omni is an open multimodal AI model that combines vision, audio, and language capabilities into a single framework. Designed to simplify development of agent-based systems, it was introduced at Nvidia GTC 2026 on April 28.

item.title: ToolMesh
item.description: ToolMesh converts any REST API into an MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool using simple YAML configuration. Instead of writing code to wrap APIs, you describe them declaratively and ToolMesh handles the rest.

item.title: Zed 1.0
item.description: Zed, the high-performance code editor built in Rust with a native UI, has reached version 1.0. The editor gained significant attention on Hacker News with over 1,700 points. It aims to provide the speed of vim with modern features and a native feel.

item.title: Zig AI Policy
item.description: The Zig programming language project has published its rationale for maintaining a firm anti-AI contribution policy. The project does not accept AI-generated code, even with human review. The policy has sparked discussion on Hacker News with 220+ points.

item.title: Zulip 12.0
item.description: Zulip 12.0 has been released, bringing a major visual redesign and performance improvements to the team chat platform. The release garnered 47 points on Hacker News.

item.title: OpenAI lands on Amazon Bedrock
item.description: OpenAI announced on April 28, 2026 that GPT-5.5, Codex, and a new Bedrock Managed Agents product are available in limited preview on AWS. The move comes one day after OpenAI and Microsoft restructured their exclusive deal, and fulfils OpenAI's obligation tied to its $50 billion AWS financing round. Enterprise customers can now access OpenAI models through existing AWS IAM credentials, PrivateLink, and CloudTrail without switching cloud providers.

item.title: Ghostty leaving GitHub
item.description: Mitchell Hashimoto—GitHub user #1299, joined February 2008—announced on April 28 that his terminal emulator Ghostty will leave GitHub over chronic reliability failures. He describes marking his journal almost every day when outages block work. No new host is confirmed yet; a read-only mirror stays at the current GitHub URL.

item.title: GitHub RCE CVE-2026-3854
item.description: Wiz Research publicly disclosed CVE-2026-3854 on April 28—a CVSS 8.7 flaw in GitHub's git push pipeline that lets any authenticated user execute arbitrary code on backend servers with a single command. GitHub.com was patched in six hours on March 4. GitHub Enterprise Server admins must upgrade to 3.19.3, 3.18.6, 3.17.12, 3.16.15, 3.15.19, or 3.14.24. At disclosure, 88% of GHES instances remained unpatched.

item.title: How ChatGPT serves ads
item.description: A researcher reverse-engineered ChatGPT's ad attribution system and published a full technical breakdown. Ads arrive as single_advertiser_ad_unit objects injected into the response stream. Four encrypted Fernet tokens handle spam integrity, forward attribution (30-day cookie), impression tracking, and server-side reconciliation. Clicks open in ChatGPT's in-app webview, where OpenAI's OAIQ SDK reports product views back to bzr.openai.com.

item.title: Who owns AI-written code?
item.description: A legal analysis published on HN (396 points, 374 comments) establishes three determinants of AI-generated code ownership: human authorship requirement (the DC Circuit's Thaler ruling makes predominantly AI-generated code uncopyrightable), work-for-hire doctrine (employers typically own code created using company tools), and GPL license contamination (models trained on copyleft code may reproduce obligations unknowingly). None is fully resolved in court.

item.title: Before GitHub
item.description: Armin Ronacher (Flask, Jinja2, Click) published a personal history of open source before GitHub's 2008 arrival. He describes a "much smaller world" where projects lived on self-hosted Trac installations, Subversion repositories, and mailing lists—and where reputation mattered "in a very direct way" because you needed to know a maintainer's track record before depending on their code. Dependency selection was deliberate; vendoring was common. GitHub eliminated the barriers to publishing and disco…

item.title: Bugs Rust won't catch
item.description: An audit of 44 CVEs in uutils (a Rust reimplementation of GNU coreutils) identifies the bug classes that escape Rust's safety guarantees entirely. The largest cluster is TOCTOU (time-of-check-time-of-use) vulnerabilities: operations spread across multiple syscalls leave windows where symlinks can redirect paths. Permission race conditions arise when directories are created with default permissions then fixed afterward—the fix is to set permissions at creation time. Path comparison failures occur…

item.title: Wire replaces Signal in Bundestag
item.description: Germany's parliament has mandated Wire as its official secure messaging platform, replacing Signal. The switch is driven by digital sovereignty concerns: Wire's servers can be self-hosted within German federal infrastructure, while Signal's backend runs on US-controlled services, creating a dependency the Bundestag considers incompatible with sensitive legislative communications. Wire uses the same Signal Protocol for end-to-end encryption but adds enterprise deployment options including on-prem…

item.title: Rocky SQL engine
item.description: Rocky is an open-source (Apache 2.0) Rust-based control plane for data warehouse pipelines. It sits above existing warehouses—Databricks, Snowflake, BigQuery, DuckDB—rather than replacing them, handling DAG orchestration, governance, and safety guarantees. The headline features are named branches (isolated pipeline testing with blast-radius analysis before merging), compiler-time column lineage (traces individual columns from downstream facts back to source seeds with no runtime overhead), and c…

item.title: Auto-Architecture: Karpathy's loop on CPU design
item.description: A project by Felipe Sens applies Karpathy's iterative development methodology—the "generate, evaluate, generate better" loop from nanoGPT and similar projects—to CPU architecture design rather than neural network design. The system runs automated tournaments where candidate CPU architectures compete on benchmark performance, and the winning characteristics seed the next generation of candidates. The project is documented as a GitHub-hosted blog post and has generated 144 HN points and 29 comment…

item.title: Claude Code malware regression
item.description: A tracked regression in Claude Managed Agents (GitHub issue #49363, 213 HN points, 109 comments) describes a system prompt that appends a malware-scanning directive to every file read operation. The agent spends tokens and billing charges performing the analysis on each read, then incorrectly refuses to write any code—even after confirming no malware exists. Users are charged for each failed session. The bug is a false positive loop: the malware reminder context bleeds into the agent's safety ev…

item.title: Tool: OpenAI on AWS Bedrock
item.description: GPT-5.5, Codex, and Bedrock Managed Agents — now accessible via your existing AWS credentials without switching cloud providers

item.title: Tool: Rocky SQL Engine
item.description: A Rust-written SQL control plane that adds Git-style branching, compile-time contracts, and column lineage to your existing data warehouse

item.title: Tool: LLaDA2.0-Uni
item.description: A diffusion large language model that unifies multimodal understanding and generation — text, vision, and image editing in one architecture (234 HF upvotes, #1 trending)

item.title: Tool: VibeVoice
item.description: Microsoft Research's long-form multi-speaker speech synthesis model using next-token diffusion and a continuous speech tokenizer (166 HF upvotes, #3 trending)

item.title: Engineering Read: Before GitHub
item.description: Armin Ronacher's "Before GitHub" and Mitchell Hashimoto's Ghostty departure, read together, describe the same arc: friction as a feature, centralisation as a trade-off, and the moment a platform's reliability costs exceed its convenience benefits.

item.title: Paper: Agentic World Modeling
item.description: As AI systems shift from generating text to accomplishing goals through sustained interaction, the ability to model environment dynamics becomes the central bottleneck. This paper proposes a "levels × laws" taxonomy: three capability levels (L1 Predictor, L2 Simulator, L3 Evolver) crossed with four governing-law regimes (physical, digital, social, scientific). The framework unifies 400+ previously isolated works and gives practitioners a concrete decision rule for selecting and evaluating world-…

item.title: Microsoft and OpenAI end exclusive deal
item.description: A $13B investment, 27% ownership, and six years of exclusivity just gave way to a multi-cloud future. OpenAI drops AGI trigger clause; Microsoft loses revenue share but keeps the IP license through 2032.

item.title: GPT-5.5 launches
item.description: OpenAI’s first fully end-to-end multimodal model processes text, images, audio, and video in one architecture. API went live April 24. Effective cost increase is ~20% once token efficiency is factored in.

item.title: Mercor data breach
item.description: Lapsus$ exploited a malicious LiteLLM release (95M monthly downloads) to harvest credentials and pivot into Mercor’s systems. Five lawsuits filed in ten days. Organizations pinning dependencies with cryptographic hashes were fully protected.

item.title: Rural data center backlash
item.description: 67% of planned AI data centers target rural land. Residents near facilities face 267% electricity bill increases. Data center cancellations due to local opposition quadrupled year-over-year. A federal moratorium bill from Sanders and AOC is pending.

item.title: Google Pentagon AI deal
item.description: Google proposes guardrails against domestic surveillance and autonomous weapons without human control—the same conditions that got Anthropic dropped from DoD contracts in March. Internal opposition echoes Project Maven in 2018.

item.title: macOS 27 networking changes
item.description: Apple finally removes the protocol it deprecated in Mavericks (2013). MDM, device enrolment, app distribution, and software update connections must meet ATS standards or break.

item.title: Talkie: vintage language model
item.description: Books, newspapers, patents, and legal documents from before 1931. Anachronism classifiers filter out post-1930 leakage. The result: a contamination-free testbed for in-context learning, future anticipation, and out-of-distribution generalization research.

item.title: NVIDIA Ising quantum AI models
item.description: A vision-language model for automated calibration plus two 3D-CNN variants for real-time error decoding. Available on GitHub, Hugging Face, and build.nvidia.com. 2.5× faster and 3× more accurate than pyMatching, the current standard.

item.title: Google employee protest Pentagon AI
item.description: The letter demands Google refuse classified military AI contracts that lack guardrails against autonomous weapons and domestic surveillance. In 2018, a similar protest forced Google to exit the DoD drone imagery project.

item.title: Claw Code open-source coding agent
item.description: Built by Sigrid Jin after the March 2026 Claude Code source leak. Six core tools: Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep. Multi-agent orchestration and tool-calling. Works with any Anthropic API key.

item.title: LiteLLM supply chain attack
item.description: Attackers poisoned two PyPI versions in 13 minutes via a compromised Trivy maintainer account. LiteLLM holds AI provider API keys for every company that uses it—making it uniquely attractive. A compliance firm certifying it was simultaneously exposed as fabricating SOC 2 reports.

item.title: GPT-5.5 API
item.description: OpenAI’s most capable agentic model, now at API pricing you can run in production

item.title: Claw Code Tool
item.description: Rust core, Python workspace. Six tools: Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep. Multi-agent orchestration. Requires only an Anthropic API key. MIT license. 172,000+ GitHub stars in weeks.

item.title: NVIDIA Ising Tool
item.description: Open-source AI models that accelerate quantum processor calibration and error correction

item.title: MarkItDown Tool
item.description: One command converts PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, HTML, images, audio, and ZIP archives to clean Markdown. MIT license. Python 3.10+. v0.1.5 released Feb 20, 2026.

item.title: The Next Two Years of Software Engineering
item.description: Addy Osmani maps the five questions that will determine which engineers thrive when AI writes the majority of code: junior pipeline collapse, skills atrophy, role evolution from coder to auditor, specialist versus T-shaped identity, and what education needs to become.

item.title: AI agent wipes production database in 9 seconds — Daily Digest 002
item.description: Jer Crane, founder of PocketOS, was using Cursor—an AI-powered code editor—with Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.6 as the underlying model. The agent was given routine infrastructure tasks alongside access to Railway, a deployment platform Crane used to host his production database.

item.title: DeepSeek V4 — Daily Digest 002
item.description: On April 24, 2026, DeepSeek released a two-model family under the MIT License. V4-Pro is a 1.6 trillion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model that activates only 49 billion parameters per token—comparable compute per call to a 50B dense model, but with the capacity of a much larger system. V4-Flash is the lighter variant: 284B total, 13B active, intended for latency-sensitive applications.

item.title: OpenAI retires SWE-bench Verified — Daily Digest 002
item.description: On February 23, 2026, OpenAI published a research post explaining why it is no longer reporting SWE-bench Verified scores for its frontier models. The post identified two fundamental problems with the benchmark at the current performance level of frontier systems.

item.title: Chrome Prompt API — Daily Digest 002
item.description: Google shipped the Prompt API for Chrome 138+, allowing web developers to send natural-language requests directly to Gemini Nano running on the user’s device. No API key, no server round-trip, no data leaves the machine. The API is available today on localhost with a flag, and via origin trial for production deployments.

item.title: TurboQuant — Daily Digest 002
item.description: TurboQuant is a vector quantization method that compresses high-dimensional vectors—KV caches, embeddings, attention keys—to 2–4 bits per coordinate while maintaining near-optimal reconstruction fidelity. It appeared as an interactive walkthrough on Hacker News and gathered 158 points.

item.title: MCP hits 97M installs — Daily Digest 002
item.description: The Model Context Protocol, Anthropic’s open standard for connecting AI agents to external tools and data sources, crossed 97 million monthly SDK downloads in March 2026. Over 10,000 active public MCP servers are now registered. Every major AI provider—OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Cohere, Mistral—ships MCP-compatible tooling as a default, not an option.

item.title: DeepSeek V4 API live — Daily Digest 002
item.description: The DeepSeek V4 API launched alongside the model release on April 24, 2026. V4-Pro (1.6T params, 49B active) and V4-Flash (284B params, 13B active) are both available. The API accepts requests in the OpenAI ChatCompletions format and the Anthropic Messages format interchangeably—switching from either provider is a base URL change and an API key swap.

item.title: Block Goose donated to Linux Foundation — Daily Digest 002
item.description: Block donated Goose to the Linux Foundation’s Agentic AI Foundation, placing it under the same neutral governance umbrella as MCP. Goose is a local-first AI agent framework written in Rust: it runs entirely on your machine, connects to external tools through MCP, and supports any LLM backend that exposes an OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic-compatible API.

item.title: Google Agent Development Kit — Daily Digest 002
item.description: Google open-sourced the Agent Development Kit (ADK) on April 9, 2026. The Python library provides multi-agent orchestration with a declarative API: define agents, tools, and the routing logic between them; ADK handles execution, state management, and structured output validation. It ships with built-in connectors for Vertex AI, Gemini, and any OpenAI-compatible API endpoint—including DeepSeek V4 and self-hosted models.

item.title: EvanFlow — Daily Digest 002
item.description: EvanFlow is a TDD (test-driven development) harness for Claude Code that structures the agent’s loop around test execution: you write a failing test, EvanFlow runs it, feeds the result back to Claude Code, and lets the agent iterate until the test passes. The cycle repeats for the next failing test. This constrains the agent to work toward concrete, verifiable outcomes rather than generating code in an unconstrained direction.

item.title: SWE-bench Pro launches — Daily Digest 002
item.description: Scale AI launched SWE-bench Pro to replace SWE-bench Verified as the standard coding benchmark for frontier AI models. The new benchmark uses harder, verified, uncontaminated problems specifically designed for the performance level of 2026 models. OpenAI recommended SWE-bench Pro in its February 2026 post announcing the retirement of SWE-bench Verified.

item.title: DeepSeek V4 API — Tool — Daily Digest 002
item.description: What it is: REST API for DeepSeek-V4-Pro and V4-Flash—MoE models with 1M-token context that match Claude Opus 4.6 SWE-bench scores at ~10× lower cost.

item.title: Google Agent Development Kit — Tool — Daily Digest 002
item.description: What it is: An open-source Python framework for building production multi-agent systems with declarative orchestration, built-in tool calling, memory persistence, and structured output.

item.title: Block Goose — Tool — Daily Digest 002
item.description: What it is: A local-first AI coding agent written in Rust, donated to the Linux Foundation. Supports MCP tools and any LLM backend. Runs entirely on your machine—no cloud dependency.

item.title: Chrome Prompt API — Tool — Daily Digest 002
item.description: What it is: A JavaScript API in Chrome 138+ that runs Gemini Nano on-device. No server, no API key, no data leaves the machine. Supports text, image, and audio input with streaming output.

item.title: AI should elevate your thinking, not replace it — Daily Digest 002
item.description: John opens with an observation that AI has created a surface-level productivity that is impossible to distinguish from genuine capability unless you probe it. Engineers can present AI-generated design decisions, architecture diagrams, and code reviews that look polished and authoritative. The problem: they cannot reproduce the reasoning, defend the tradeoffs, or spot when the AI was wrong.

item.description: A model too capable for public release — and what that means for the AI security era

item.title: Daily Digest 001 — DeepSeek V4
item.description: Open weights, a 10x KV cache reduction, and pricing at $0.14/M tokens resets expectations for what open-source models can do

item.title: Daily Digest 001 — Amateur solves Erdos problem with ChatGPT
item.description: GPT-5.4 found a path through a formula that professional mathematicians had collectively missed for six decades

item.title: Daily Digest 001 — OpenAI retires SWE-bench Verified
item.description: Top models now score above 80% on tasks designed to be hard — the benchmark saturated faster than any evaluation infrastructure could keep pace

item.title: Daily Digest 001 — DeepMind Decoupled DiLoCo
item.description: Asynchronous distributed training reaches 88% goodput in high-failure environments where synchronous methods collapse to 27%

item.title: Daily Digest 001 — Thoughtworks Tech Radar: AI Forces Return to Fundamentals
item.description: Martin Fowler's Fragments post from April 21 distills the headline finding from the 34th Technology Radar: amid the AI goldrush, Thoughtworks' engineering advisory council is moving toward the practices teams abandoned in the sprint to ship — pair programming, rigorous mutation testing, DORA metrics, zero-trust architecture. The implication is uncomfortable: AI-assisted development accelerates output, but it also accelerates the accumulation of every bad habit your team already had.

item.title: Daily Digest 001 — Paper: Thinking with Reasoning Skills
item.description: Researchers from the ACL 2026 industry track present a method for training language models to selectively engage extended chain-of-thought reasoning only for problems that genuinely require it. The result: fewer tokens on easy tasks, no accuracy regression on hard tasks, and a practical training recipe that can be applied to any instruction-tuned base model. The paper lands at exactly the moment practitioners are asking whether reasoning models' verbosity is a cost problem or a quality problem. …
